children: By Phuong Nguyen and Mas Alina Arifin

Vietnam's domestic coffee prices continued to fall this week, following a consecutive drop in the London market from last week, while premiums were higher in Indonesia amid lower supplies, traders said on Thursday.
Farmers in the Central Highlands, Vietnam's coffee belt, sold beans at 74,200 dong to 75,000 dong ($2.88 to $2.91) per kg, down from last week's 83,200 dong to 83,800 dong range
settled down $52, or 2%, at $3,019 a metric ton on Wednesday, its lowest level since mid-January 2024, according to LSEG data.
"Expectations of increased global supplies are weighing on prices with Vietnam harvest underway and weak Brazilian real encouraging exports," said a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City.

Another trader based in the Central Highlands said rising input and labour costs, together with increasingly erratic weather, have reduced profitability and may discourage many farmers from investing in their crops
"The sunny weather this year has favoured natural coffee drying; many exporters and traders purchase only naturally sun-dried this harvest's coffee beans," the second trader added
In Indonesia, Sumatra robusta coffee beans were offered at a premium of $300 to $365 to the December contract due to lower bean supplies, a trader said
Another trader quoted a $350 premium to the November contract, up from $300 last week
